newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to allow bond issues for foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to allow bond issues for foreign investors.

text.p: South Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it would allow three small companies to issue 31 billion won in bonds to be exclusively offered to foreign investors.

The commission said in a statement Korea Exchange Bank (KEB) Leasing Co Ltd submitted an application for 18 billion won of bond issues. The bonds carry a 10 percent coupon rate and an 11.3-12.0 percent yield, with a three-year maturity.
Cho Hung Leasing Co Ltd applied for eight billion won worth, which will carry a 10 percent coupon rate and an 11.4-119 percent yield.
EZ Tech Co Ltd will issue five billion won worth of bonds with a 11.5-12.0 percent coupon rate and a 12.0-12.11 percent yield.
South Korea allowed foreign investors to buy bonds issued by small firms from January 1997.
Eight companies have issued 114 billion won worth of bonds as of Monday, the commission said. This excludes the three companies to be approved on Tuesday.
